tip.title: aimer + infinitive
tip.body: To say what you like doing, use aimer + the infinitive: J'aime lire (I like reading). Je + aime becomes J'aime — the e drops before a vowel. In the negative, ne… pas wraps around the conjugated verb: Je n'aime pas danser. In speech many people drop the ne: J'aime pas danser.

tip.title: On y va ?
tip.body: In everyday French, on (literally "one") usually means "we": On va au cinéma ? = Shall we go to the cinema? Just raise your voice at the end to make it a suggestion. To decline politely: Désolé, je ne peux pas (a woman writes désolée — it sounds the same).

tip.title: Combien de fois ?
tip.body: Answer Tu fais ça souvent ? (Do you do that often?) with une fois, deux fois, trois fois par semaine — once, twice, three times a week — or souvent (often), de temps en temps (from time to time), le week-end (at weekends). Note: le samedi means "on Saturdays", samedi alone means "this Saturday".

tip.title: Like it? Use le / la. Do it? Use du / de la.
tip.body: aimer, adorer, préférer and détester take an infinitive (J'adore nager) or a noun with le / la / les for things in general: J'aime le sport, je déteste le foot. For sports and activities use faire de: je fais du judo, de la danse, de l'escalade. jouer à is for games and ball sports (je joue au tennis, aux cartes) and jouer de is for instruments (je joue du piano, de la guitare). After ne… pas, du / de la become de: je ne fais pas de sport. Remember à + le = au, de + le = du.

culture.title: Pétanque, the Tour & hockey
culture.body: In France, pétanque comes from the south: players throw metal balls (boules) as close as possible to a small wooden ball, the cochonnet, often in a village square on a summer evening. Every July the Tour de France cycling race crosses the country, traditionally finishing in Paris (in 2024 it ended in Nice because of the Paris Olympics), and crowds line the roads shouting Allez ! Cycling is also hugely popular in Belgium, and in Switzerland many people ski and hike. In Québec, hockey is the passion: children play on outdoor rinks in winter, and fans follow the Montréal Canadiens.
